newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia unlikely to meet jobs forecast - Costello.
newsitem.headline: Australia unlikely to meet jobs forecast - Costello.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Sunday the government was unlikely to meet its forecast that unemployment would fall to 8.5 percent by the June quarter, but said unemployment would be much improved by June 1998.

"Probably it won't be eight and a half by the end of the (1996/97) year, but I can promise you this - it will be much better by June of 1998, it will be substantially better," Costello told the Nine Network's Sunday program.
Figures last week showed unemployment remained stuck at 8.7 percent in April, although employment rose by 37,100.
The government increased its June 1997 unemployment forecast to 8.5 percent at the January mid-year review compared with the 8.25 percent forecast in August last year.
Unemployment has been stuck at or above 8.5 percent for the past year.
"What we're now seeing is increased jobs coming through; it was 37,000 in the last month," Costello said.

"We've got three interest rate cuts in place, we've got better industrial relations, we're solving our debt and savings problems, and we have a quite optimistic growth potential over the course of the next year."

Australian Treasury Secretary Ted Evans said last week there was little chance the government would meet its forecast for employment growth of 1.5 percent in 1996/97 (July-June) and an unemployment rate of 8.5 percent by the June quarter.
Costello said the government's 1997/98 budget, to be announced next Tuesday, would help boost economic and jobs growth.
"The measures that we're putting in place will allow our economy to grow faster," he said.
"That means we can create more jobs, and that means that living standards can and will rise over the course of this term."
Costello said the government's main aim was to build the economy, provide jobs, bring interest rates down, make housing more affordable and get small business going.
